problem.value: Instruction tuning using machine-generated data is less explored in the multimodal field.

evidence.quote: Instruction tuning large language models (LLMs) using machine-generated instruction-following data has been shown to improve zero-shot capabilities on new tasks, but the idea is less explored in the multimodal field.

problem.value: There is a general lack of vision-language instruction-following data.

evidence.quote: One key challenge is the lack of vision-language instruction-following data.

contributions.value: We present a pipeline to convert image-text pairs into an instruction-following format using GPT models.

evidence.quote: We present a data reformation perspective and pipeline to convert image-text pairs into an appropriate instruction-following format, using ChatGPT/GPT-4.

contributions.value: We develop a large multimodal model by connecting a visual encoder with a language decoder and fine-tuning it end-to-end.

evidence.quote: We develop a large multimodal model (LMM), by connecting the open-set visual encoder of CLIP [40] with the language decoder Vicuna [9], and fine-tuning end-to-end on our generated instructional vision-language data.

contributions.value: We introduce LLaVA-Bench with two challenging benchmarks and diverse annotations.

evidence.quote: We present LLaVA-Bench with two challenging benchmarks, with a diverse selection of paired images, instructions and detailed annotations.

contributions.value: We release the generated multimodal instruction data, codebase, model checkpoints, and demo to the public.

evidence.quote: We release the following assets to the public: the generated multimodal instruction data, the codebase, the model checkpoints, and a visual chat demo.

task.value: Multimodal language-image instruction-following and general-purpose visual and language understanding.

evidence.quote: By instruction tuning on such generated data, we introduce LLaVA: Large Language and Vision Assistant, an end-to-end trained large multimodal model that connects a vision encoder and an LLM for generalpurpose visual and language understanding.

method_summary.value: We choose Vicuna as our language model and the pre-trained CLIP visual encoder ViT-L/14 to extract visual features.

evidence.quote: We choose Vicuna [9] as our LLM f ϕ (•) parameterized by ϕ, as it has the best instruction following capabilities in language tasks among publicly available checkpoints [48,9,38].

method_summary.value: A simple linear projection layer connects image features into the word embedding space by applying a trainable matrix W.

evidence.quote: Specifically, we apply a trainable projection matrix W to convert Z v into language embedding tokens H v , which have the same dimensionality as the word embedding space in the language model:

method_summary.value: The model is trained using the original auto-regressive training objective of the LLM on the prediction tokens of the assistant answers.

evidence.quote: We perform instruction-tuning of the LLM on the prediction tokens, using its original auto-regressive training objective.

method_summary.value: Stage 1 pre-training freezes both the visual encoder and LLM weights, optimizing only the projection matrix for feature alignment using filtered image-text pairs.

evidence.quote: In training, we keep both the visual encoder and LLM weights frozen, and maximize the likelihood of (3) with trainable parameters θ = W (the projection matrix) only.

method_summary.value: Stage 2 fine-tuning keeps the visual encoder frozen while updating both the projection layer and the LLM weights end-to-end on multimodal instruction-following data.

evidence.quote: We always keep the visual encoder weights frozen, and continue to update both the pre-trained weights of the projection layer and LLM in LLaVA; i.e., the trainable parameters are θ = {W, ϕ} in (3).

limitations.value: Assessment challenges due to combining language and visual tasks

evidence.quote: Assessing the performance of LLaVA is challenging as it involves both language and visual tasks.

future_work.value: Inspiration for future research on more capable multimodal models

evidence.quote: We hope our work can inspire future research on building more capable multimodal models.

future_work.value: Evaluating robustness and unexplored aspects of GPT-4 based multimodal evaluation

evidence.quote: While text-only GPT-4 based multimodal evaluation is consistent and accurate in our study, its robustness in different situations and capability to evaluate other unexplored aspects are subjects for future work.

ethics.value: Deployment and release of LLaVA bring both potential benefits and risks

evidence.quote: The broader impact of LLaVA, a general-purpose visual assistant, has potential benefits and risks associated with its deployment and release.

ethics.value: Precautionary measures used to minimize malicious input risks

evidence.quote: To minimize potential misuse and harmful consequences, we employ two precautionary measures for LLaVA: (1) OpenAI Filter API for user input text to prevent harmful or inappropriate text instructions from being processed by the model, and (2) NSFW Filter for uploaded user images to detect and block Not Safe For Work (NSFW) content or any other potentially harmful image inputs.
This raises concerns about inferences made, especially in critical applications (e.g., medical).

ethics.value: Transfer of bias from base models leading to unfair representations

evidence.quote: Bias can be transferred from the base models to LLaVA, both from the vision encoder (CLIP) and the language decoder (LLaMA/Vicuna).

ethics.value: Energy consumption concerns when scaling up datasets or model sizes

evidence.quote: Though energy consumption is not a primary concern for LLaVA due to a smaller pretraining dataset (see details in Sec. C), it may become a concern when scaling up the pretraining dataset or increasing the model size, e.g., to a larger LLaMA version like the 65B model.

claims.value: LLaVA yields an 85.1% relative score compared with GPT-4 on a synthetic multimodal instruction-following dataset.

evidence.quote: Our experiments show that LLaVA demonstrates impressive multimodal chat abilities, sometimes exhibiting the behaviors of multimodal GPT-4 on unseen images/instructions, and yields a 85.1% relative score compared with GPT-4 on a synthetic multimodal instruction-following dataset.

claims.value: When fine-tuned on Science QA, LLaVA and GPT-4 achieve a new state-of-the-art accuracy of 92.53%.

evidence.quote: When fine-tuned on Science QA, the synergy of LLaVA and GPT-4 achieves a new state-of-the-art accuracy of 92.53%.
